text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hongkongers become rulers of their own house after more than one-and-a-half centuries when former shipping tycoon Tung Chee Hwa is sworn in as Special Administrative Region's first chief executive.
- China shakes off 155 years of humiliation inflicted by foreign powers when, in solemn ceremony telecast live around world, it takes back sovereignty over Hong Kong from Britain.

- The market value of all stocks listed on Stock Exchange of Singapore eases marginally in first half of year despite current market downturn which wipes Singapore $10 billion off Singapore Telecom's market capitalisation.
- Singaporeans may soon be able to shop on Internet and not worry about security of their transactions -- thanks to new electronic commerce payment gateway.

- China's President Jiang Zemin pledges to 6.5 million Hongkongers his government will "unswervingly implement the basic policies of one country, two systems" when he launches Hongkong Special Administrative Region of China and ends 156 years of British colonial rule.

- Almost S$5 billion raised in local stockmarket in last six months but that was more than wiped out by declines in share prices, leaving total market capitalisation of Singapore bourse some 2.5 percent smaller.
- Sembawang Corp subsidiary Resources Development Corp will acquire 30 affiliated companies for S$100 million in an exercise aimed at turning it into Sembawang's property arm.
- Scotts Holdings saga takes another surprise turn with announcement company and its chief executive officer, Chng Hee Kok, have mutually agreed to part ways.
- Malaysian businessman Soh Chee Wen will underwrite three-quarters of Inno-Pacific Holdings' rights issue in unusual move that could lead to general offer.

- Bonvests Holdings and Compact Metal Industries separately announce plans to respectively issue 63.42 million and 59.44 million warrants on three-for-10 basis in conjunction with transferable loan facilities they are getting from DBS Bank.
